images.caption: Figure 2:Overview ofHeave-Ho. At the high level, the leader’s vision-language planner selects the next team skill from its camera and speaks it; every follower recognizes the command on board, and all robots start it on a shared skill schedule. At the low level, each robot maps the team skill to its own role, generates a reference conditioned on the object specification, and tracks it with a frozen foundation tracking model plus a residual policy shared by all robots. No network message is exchanged between robots.
Figure 3:Leader’s head-camera views over a task, each with the team skill chosen at that step: the narrow door in the real world (top) and the box handover in simulation (bottom).

Figure 4:The tasks ofHH-Benchin simulation. Bottom: tasks can be chained into longer ones, here a stair carry, a placement on a dolly, and a handover of a second box to a third robot. Time sequences are in App.B.2and videos on theproject page.

Figure 5:Real-world experiments. The first four rows show two G1 robots over time, from left to right, labeled with the team skill being executed. The last row shows teams that differ from the training configuration, including a different humanoid and people. Faces are obscured for anonymity. Full time sequences of all teams are in App.C.2and videos on theproject page.
Figure 7:Train with two, deploy with many. The policy trained with two G1 robots (top left) carries a table in simulation with teams of four, eight, and ten robots, without retraining.
Figure 8:Head camera mount. (a) A ZED stereo camera on the head of a G1. (b, c) The two 3D-printed parts of the mount.
Figure 9:Real-world time sequences of the teams shown as single frames inFig.5, and of the team of three G1 robots and a person. Time runs from left to right. Faces are obscured for anonymity.
Figure 10:Time sequences of the lift-and-carry tasks inHH-Bench, in simulation. Time runs from left to right.
Figure 11:Time sequences of the handover, shoulder-carry, pull, and push tasks inHH-Bench, in simulation. Time runs from left to right.
